newsitem.title: USA: ARCO to boost spot crude buying over 5 years.
newsitem.headline: ARCO to boost spot crude buying over 5 years.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) plans to buy more crude oil from outside companies over the next five years to offset declining output from Alaskan fields, a company executive told Reuters.

As the company's Alaskan production falls -- down six percent last year -- the company plans to feed its growing refining capacity by buying more foreign crudes and squeezing its older Alaskan fields with new technology.
In five years, ARCO's total purchases of crude will amount to 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) from its current 20,000 bpd, said Bill Rusnack, president of ARCO Products Co told Reuters.
"100,000 barrels-per-day of crude will be purchased from people other than ARCO," Rusnack said.
ARCO's two West Coast refineries run a combined 475,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude, up from 440,000 two years ago due to mechanical upgrades.
The company now runs about 20,000 bpd of Canadon Seco, an Argentine lookalike to Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, ARCO's staple.
After experimenting with other crudes, ARCO has stuck with Canadon Seco because it yields good quality calcined coke which ARCO sells worldwide as a component of aluminum.
Rusnack said the calcined coke market will determine how much Canadon Seco ARCO uses in the future.
But in the foreseeable future, ARCO expects ANS to remain its primary crude.
"Honestly, I hope our Alaskan people find and produce more," Rusnack said.
